analysis.title: Coffee Break: Inflation expectations in the US: markets vs. consumers
key_insights: October US CPI came in stronger than expected and yoy inflation accelerated to around 4%. The short end of the UST curve sold off sharply after the print.
Market-based inflation expectations barely moved after the CPI data. The 5Y USD inflation swap is around 2.35%, close to its low this year, and breakeven rates show a similar picture.
The report reads the subdued market-based expectations as the market treating the inflation spike as temporary and trusting the Fed to contain price pressure and protect its credibility.
The survey of professional forecasters (SPF) sees inflation at 2.6% over the next five years, in line with the swap market. Both point to a return to 2% or lower after a few months above target.

The NY Fed consumer survey shows inflation expectations of 3.3% over the next three years, and the University of Michigan survey also shows expectations above 2%. Consumer expectations usually run above market and SPF measures because of cognitive biases, such as overweighting food and gasoline prices or demanding compensation for uncertainty.

Consumer expectations were closer to realised inflation than market and SPF measures in recent years. In November 2023 consumers expected 3% inflation over three years, which proved accurate. The author attributes this to coincidence, since the recent acceleration came mostly from the war on Iran.
Energy prices are off their recent peak but well above early-year levels. WTI is at USD 90/bbl against USD 60/bbl at the start of 2026.
If inflation stays well above 2% in 2027, a 5Y inflation swap of 2.3% implies inflation below 2% over 2028-31. That would resemble 2012-16, which is not the author's baseline scenario.
With 5Y real yields at 2.5%, which the report calls historically high, the author finds USD inflation-linked bonds rather appealing.

macro_indicators.interpretation: October CPI was stronger than expected and yoy inflation accelerated. Short-end UST yields sold off, while market-based inflation expectations did not react.
Close to this year's low. The report reads it as the market treating the inflation spike as temporary and trusting the Fed.
Consistent with swaps. Implies inflation returning to around 2% after a few months above target.

macro_indicators.indicator: NY Fed consumer inflation expectations, 3Y ahead
macro_indicators.interpretation: Consumers expect more persistent inflation than markets or professional forecasters.
Down from its recent peak but well above the USD 60/bbl level at the start of 2026.
Historically high, which makes USD inflation-linked bonds appealing in the author's view.

trade_ideas.rationale: The 5Y inflation swap at 2.3% implies inflation below 2% over 2028-31, which is not the author's baseline, and 5Y real yields are historically high at 2.5%.

risk_factors: Inflation stays well above 2% through 2027 and beyond, which would make current market-based expectations too low.
Loose fiscal policy, harsher tariffs and renewed geopolitical tensions keep price pressure elevated.
Energy prices remain significantly above early-2026 levels.
charts_described: Chart compares average realised yoy CPI inflation 3Y ahead, NY Fed consumer inflation expectations 3Y ahead, the 3Y USD inflation swap and SPF 5Y-ahead inflation expectations from 2010 to 2026. A callout says consumer expectations have recently been most aligned with realised inflation.
vol_and_positioning: The sell-off at the short end of the UST curve after the CPI print contrasts with unchanged long-horizon inflation swaps and breakevens.
geopolitical: The recent acceleration in inflation was mostly due to the war on Iran, which pushed up energy prices.
Loose fiscal policy, harsher tariffs and renewed geopolitical tensions under Trump 2.0 are cited as inflationary.

tension_points.bull_case: Market-based expectations (5Y swap around 2.35%) and the SPF (2.6% over five years) point to inflation returning to 2% or lower after a temporary spike, with the Fed containing price pressure.
tension_points.bear_case: Consumer expectations (NY Fed 3.3% over three years) stay well above 2%, and consumers were closer to realised inflation in recent years. Loose fiscal policy, tariffs and geopolitical tensions could keep inflation high.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation staying well above 2% in 2027 would make a 5Y swap at 2.3% imply inflation below 2% over 2028-31, which the report does not treat as its baseline.
